key_insight: An expert-derived causal AI model estimated early fluid and vasopressor doses for septic shock that acted like an informative treatment policy in validation.
clinical_relevance: This could help ICU teams better individualize early haemodynamic management in septic shock, but it is not yet proof that following the recommendations improves patient outcomes.
method: Built a graphical causal inference model grounded in clinician knowledge to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects.
Trained on 1,706 MIMIC ICU admissions and externally validated on 1,450 eICU admissions.
Compared model recommendations against observed fluid and vasopressor dosing over the first 6 ICU hours.
evidence_signal: Across 3,156 patients, external validation showed AUROCs of 0.72 for survival and 0.70 for clinical improvement, with treatment effects varying by baseline physiology.
watch_item: Recommendations were validated observationally, so confounding by indication remains a concern and prospective testing is still needed before clinical use.
paper_title: The Causal Artificial Intelligence Clinician for early haemodynamic management of septic shock in ICU
